overview: After 1.b4 c6 Black prepares ...d5 and ...Qb6 or ...a5 against the b4-pawn, a Slav-like set-up. White fianchettoes with 2.Bb2 and plays a3 or b5 ideas, aiming for flank play and the long diagonal. The most played sub-line is the Schuehler Gambit 2.Bb2 a5 3.b5, but the quieter 3.b5 cxb5 or 3.a3 axb4 lines are the less committal choice. The game is positional and flank-based.

white_ideas.idea: Fianchetto the queen bishop on b2 and hit e5 and g7
Gain queenside space with a3, b5 or c4
Develop with Nf3, e3, Be2 and castle

black_ideas.idea: Build a Slav-style centre with ...d5, ...Nf6 and ...e6
Develop the c8 bishop freely before closing the e6 pawn in

typical_structures.structure: Asymmetrical flank structure with White pawn on b4 or a3 and Black pawns on c6/d5
Open a-file or b-file after ...a5 and bxa5 trades

character.notes: Slow flank play with no early forcing tactics, apart from the Schuehler Gambit sideline.

gambit.notes: The main 2.Bb2 line gives no material; the Schuehler Gambit 3.b5 cxb5 is a sub-line.

soundness.notes: Sound but gives Black an easy game; no refutation.

structure.notes: Centre not fixed; White works from the flank with the bishop on b2, so flexible.

approach.notes: Rare at the top, chosen for surprise; ...c6 is one of the less common replies.

level.notes: Few forced lines; the hard part is choosing the right plan against a Slav-style set-up.

sublines_that_differ.name: Schuehler Gambit
sublines_that_differ.how: White offers the b-pawn for open lines and quick development; a gambit unlike the main quiet line.

character.reason: Slow flank play, neither particularly safe nor sharp.

gambit.reason: The main line keeps material level; the gambit is a sub-line.

soundness.reason: No refutation, only a modest edge for Black.

structure.reason: A flank opening where the centre is not yet settled.

approach.reason: Rare among strong players and chosen mainly for surprise.

plans.reason: Bb2 on the long diagonal and queenside pawn pushes.
